overview: This 449-page file traces Japanese naval transports and training ships visiting U.S. and Hawaiian ports in 1938–1940. Diplomatic requests, interdepartmental approvals, and schedule changes sit alongside confidential oil-shipment exchanges, disputes over cargo and customs rules, crew shore leave, port courtesies, and complaints about shipboard conduct. It also includes a 1919 report on Japanese vessel activity in the Philippines.
interest: The file reveals routine diplomacy alongside oil intelligence, contested cargo rules, and tensions over Japanese vessels’ conduct.
